name: lab65_win11_nmap_positive_evidence
description: Windows 11 24H2 (DESKTOP-34M18MB) on LAN; ports where nmap returned POSITIVE evidence.
labeling_note:
LABELING RULE: a port is labeled ONLY where nmap observed positive evidence -- syn-ack (open) or conn-refused (closed). Ports where nmap observed only SILENCE are EXCLUDED, not labeled `filtered`.

Why: this host rate-limits its RSTs under load. A single nmap run over all 1121 ports called 1101 ports `filtered`; chunked runs still called 218 `filtered` while this scanner held errno ECONNREFUSED (a real RST) for the same ports. An RST is positive proof of reachability; silence is absence of evidence. Labeling those ports from the validator's silence would encode the validator's own false negatives as ground truth and punish the correct answer. A corpus is only as good as the regime its validator ran in.
